what: Adaptive Biotechnologies reads the immune system’s genetic code. Its main product, clonoSEQ, measures minimal residual disease (tiny traces of cancer left after treatment) in blood cancers such as multiple myeloma and leukaemia, and it also sells immune-sequencing data and services to drug developers.
customers: Oncologists and hospitals that test patients with blood cancers, and pharmaceutical companies that use its tests in clinical trials.
money: Tests that measure residual cancer in blood cancer patients, paid by insurers and Medicare.
Sequencing services and data for drug developers.
moat: clonoSEQ is the only FDA-cleared test of its kind for several blood cancers and is built into many clinical trials, which makes it a standard that doctors and drug companies rely on.
risks: The company has lost money every year, though losses have narrowed.
Insurance coverage and Medicare reimbursement rates decide how profitable each test is.
Competitors are developing their own MRD tests.
Shareholders’ equity of $176M is small after years of losses.
opportunities: Revenue jumped from $179M in 2024 to $277M in 2025 and $298M over the last twelve months.
Cash burn fell from $254M in 2021 to about $9M over the last twelve months: the business is close to break-even.
More cancer types and more routine use of MRD testing could grow volumes for years.
Seven analysts rate it a strong buy with an average target of $34.
watch: clonoSEQ test volume growth and the timing of sustained profitability.
view: Adaptive has reached the point that matters for a diagnostics company: revenue is growing fast and cash burn has almost disappeared, from over $250 million a year in 2021 to about $9 million over the last twelve months. That changes the risk profile completely, because it no longer needs to raise money to survive.

At $4.7 billion, the market pays about 16 times revenue for a company that has just reached break-even. That is a high price, and it assumes clonoSEQ becomes routine in the treatment of blood cancers. The trend supports that, but competition is coming.
This turns on clonoSEQ adoption. I think the business is real and improving, but at this valuation most of the good news is priced in. I would wait for a pullback.
bull: MRD testing becomes standard care and clonoSEQ volumes keep compounding.
bear: Competition and reimbursement pressure slow growth before the company earns much profit.
